identification: English Yorkshire/Nottinghamshire-type high-back Windsor armchair, c1840-1870: steam-bent hoop back with nine spindles and a central pierced vase splat (urn-and-scroll piercings), bent arm bow on ring-turned baluster arm supports, solid saddle seat with strong elm grain, ring-and-baluster turned legs joined by a crinoline (crescent) stretcher with side spurs. Dark old surface, seat worn pale; arms and spindles look ash or elm, legs darker (fruitwood/elm/ash possible). Catalogue says oak and elm; I see no clear yew colour (no orange/red cast). Estimate 200-300; current bid about A$450 (next increment 470), so the room already rates it.

viewing_check: Timber of arms, spindles and legs (yew is orange-red with tight dark grain and small knots; ash is pale and open-grained; fruitwood is dark and close); crinoline stretcher original and tight; arm-bow and hoop joints, splits in the splat, worm in the legs, old repairs or later screws under the seat.
